boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen North Anna record (May 23-26, 1864) in Grant's Overland Campaign [May-June 1864]. The May 21 Spotsylvania rear-guard action and the Milford crossing precede it, and Wilson's Wharf (VA056, May 24) is a separate record on the James. Campaign-wide marches, captures, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Armies and the live field zero. Humphreys lists reinforcements reaching Lee at Hanover Junction: Hoke's brigade at 1,200 effective (Taylor), Breckinridge most probably 2,500, and Pickett 5,000 by the best information, 8,700 muskets in all; he disputes Badeau's 9,162 for Pickett. He estimates Hancock's force at not over 24,000 infantry and says Lee might have attacked it with about 36,000.
claims.rationale: Reinforcements and Humphreys' estimates, not opening strengths; the Pickett figures conflict. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 4,000 total; the live field reads 5,140 (US 2,623; CS 2,517). Humphreys gives the medical director's 2,100 Army of the Potomac wounded for May 21–26, and the Medical and Surgical History's 223 killed, 1,460 wounded and 290 missing for May 23–27, preferring the former; he says the Jericho Mills killed and wounded were probably equal on both sides.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Humphreys' two Union figures cover different dates and categories.

open_questions: Meade's North Anna paragraph is partly garbled in OCR. Lee's reports, Hill's, Warren's, Hancock's and Burnside's reports, and the compiled returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan, and it shares headquarters papers with Meade's and Sheridan's reports. Meade's, Sheridan's, Hampton's, Butler's and Wild's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXXVI, Parts 1 and 2, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
